name: Vasukai AI Visibility
author: vasukai

sections.description:
People now ask ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude and Perplexity who to buy from. Those assistants can only recommend a business whose website they have read. Vasukai AI Visibility shows you, inside WordPress, which of your pages they read and which they skip.

It does not generate files or change what crawlers see. It records AI crawler visits as they happen and reports on them, per crawler and per page.

  • AI crawler visits. A dashboard box counts visits from 19 AI crawlers, including GPTBot, OAI-SearchBot, ChatGPT-User, ClaudeBot, Claude-SearchBot, PerplexityBot, Google-Extended, Meta-ExternalAgent and Amazonbot, for the last 7 and 28 days.
  • What each visit is for. Every crawler is labelled: AI search, fetched for an answer, or model training.
  • Pages read most. The pages AI crawlers request most often.
  • Per post and page. An “AI crawlers” column on your Posts and Pages lists shows when each one was last read and by which assistants, for example “Read 24 Nov by ChatGPT, Claude”.
  • Content no AI crawler has read. A list of your latest published posts and pages that no AI crawler has requested in the last 28 days, so you know which pages assistants cannot be drawing on.
  • robots.txt check. Warns you if robots.txt turns an AI crawler away from your whole site.

Everything above works without an account and without sending any data off your site.

Optional: history in a Vasukai account

If you paste a Vasukai API key, visits are also sent to your Vasukai account for longer history and trends. This is off until you add a key. See “External services” below.

External services

This plugin can connect to Vasukai (https://www.vasukai.com), an AI visibility service. The connection is optional and off by default.

  • Only if you paste a Vasukai API key in Settings, AI Visibility: once an hour the plugin sends, for each AI crawler visit, the crawler’s name, the page path, the response status, the time and your site’s host name to https://www.vasukai.com/api/ingest/logs. Visitor IP addresses and full user agents are never sent. Visits from people are never recorded or sent.
  • Without an API key nothing is sent to Vasukai.
  • The settings page and dashboard box contain a link to a free check on vasukai.com. Nothing is sent unless you click it.

To run the robots.txt check, the plugin requests your own site’s robots.txt once an hour.

Vasukai terms: https://www.vasukai.com/terms
Vasukai privacy policy: https://www.vasukai.com/privacy
sections.installation:
1. In WordPress, go to Plugins, Add New Plugin, search for “Vasukai AI Visibility”, then click Install Now and Activate.
  2. Open Dashboard to see the AI crawler visits box. Counting starts when the plugin is switched on.
  3. Go to Settings, AI Visibility for 28 days of visits, the pages read most, content not read and the robots.txt check. The AI crawlers column appears on your Posts and Pages lists.
sections.faq:
I see no visits yet.

Counting starts when the plugin is switched on. Most sites see the first AI crawler visits within a few days.

Are the numbers complete?

The plugin counts visits that reach WordPress. If a page cache or CDN answers a crawler first, that visit is not counted, so real numbers can be higher. They are never lower than shown.

Why does a page show “Not read” when I know it is popular?

The column shows AI crawlers only, not people or search engines. A page can have plenty of human visitors and still not have been requested by any AI crawler in the last 28 days. A page cache or CDN can also answer a crawler before WordPress runs; those visits are not counted.

When does the list of unread content appear?

After a week of counting, so a newly installed plugin does not report every page as unread.

Does this slow my site down?

No. For visitors the plugin does one user agent comparison. It only writes to the database when an AI crawler visits.

Does it block AI crawlers?

No. It shows you who visits. If you want to block a crawler, edit robots.txt.
sections.changelog:
1.1.0

  • New: an AI crawlers column on the Posts and Pages lists, with the date each was last read and by which assistants.
  • New: a list of published posts and pages no AI crawler has read in the last 28 days.
  • Removed: llms.txt. The plugin now only records and reports AI crawler visits.

1.0.0

  • First release: AI crawler visits, pages read most, llms.txt and the robots.txt check.
